column9: The number of cpu cycles when the thread is not in halt state.
The number of 64-byte instruction cache lines fulfilled from the L2 cache.
The number of instructions retired from execution. This count includes exceptions and interrupts. Each exception or interrupt is counted as one instruction.
The number of branch instructions retired. This includes all types of architectural control flow changes, including exceptions and interrupts.
The number of retired branch instructions, that were mispredicted.Note that only EX direct mispredicts and indirect target mispredicts are counted.

column3: The average number of retired instructions per CPU Cycle. The lower IPC value means the application consumes more cycles due to  cache misses, branch mispredictions, pipeline stalls, I/O or any other performance bottlenecks.

The average number of CPU cycles consumed to retire an instruction. This metric is computed as the ratio of CYCLES_NOT_IN_HALT to RETIRED_INST event. The higher values means the application consumes more CPU cycles to retire an instruction due to high cache misses, branch mispredictions, pipeline stalls, I/O or any other bottlenecks. If the CPI values exceeds a threshold value, it will be highlighted in pink.
The number of retired branch instructions per thousand retired instructions.
The number of retired mispredicted branches per thousand retired instructions. Branch mispredictions incur significant performance penalty and this metric value should be reduced.
The percentage of retired mispredicted branches with respect to the total number of retired branches.
This metric is computed as retired mispredicted branches divided by the total number of retired instructions.
This metric is computed as retired mispredicted branches divided by the total number of retired branch instructions.
The number of retired branch instructions rate. This metric is computed as retired branches divided by the total number of retired instructions.
